samples.xml_description:
<module id="LFSR">
    <description>A 4-bit Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst">Active-high reset signal for initialization.</input>
        <output id="out" width_description="[3:0]">Output data representing the current state of the LFSR.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        The LFSR is a 4-bit linear feedback shift register (LFSR) designed to generate pseudo-random sequences.
        
        Input ports:
            clk: Clock signal for synchronization.
            rst: Active-high reset signal for initialization.
        
        Output ports:
            out [3:0]: 4-bit output representing the current state of the LFSR.
        
        On the rising edge of the clock (clk), if the reset (rst) is high, the register is initialized to 0000.
        Otherwise, the bits in the register are shifted left, and the new feedback value is inserted at the LSB.
        
        Feedback calculation: Feedback = ~(out[3] ^ out[2])
    </implementation>
</module>
